chunks: And as for that which indicates the invalidity of the sect of the Waqifiya, who stopped at the Imamate of Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him),

and said: 'He is the Mahdi,' their statement is false due to what has become manifest of his death (peace be upon him), which became widely known and circulated, just as the death of his father, his grandfather, and those of his forefathers who preceded him (peace be upon them all) became widely known.

And if we were to doubt [his death], we would not be distinguished from the Nawusiyya, the Kaisaniyya, the Ghulat, and the Mufawwidha, who disputed the death of those of their forefathers who preceded him (peace be upon them all).
Furthermore, his death became widely known to a greater extent than the death of any of his forefathers (peace be upon them all), because it was more apparent and present, with judges and witnesses.
And a proclamation was made for him in Baghdad on the bridge, and it was said: 'This is the one whom the Rafidha claim is alive and will not die, has died a natural death.'
And what occurred in this manner is a fact that cannot be disputed.

key_terms.إِمَامَة: Imamate, the leadership and spiritual authority of the Imams
key_terms.الوَاقِفَة: Waqifiya, a sect that stopped believing in the death of an Imam, claiming he is the Mahdi
key_terms.الْكَيسَانِيَّة: Kaisaniyya, a sect believing in Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيّ: The Mahdi, the guided one expected to reappear
key_terms.الْمُفَوَّضَة: Mufawwidha, a sect believing in the delegation of divine attributes
key_terms.حَتْفَ أَنْفِهِ: A natural death, as opposed to martyrdom or violent death

ai.seo_question: How does Shia scholarship refute the Waqifiya belief in the immortality of Imam Musa al-Kadim?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi argues that the Waqifiya's claim of Imam Musa al-Kadhim's immortality is invalidated by the widespread, public confirmation of his death in Baghdad, witnessed by judges and the general populace. This historical certainty distinguishes his passing from the ambiguous or denied deaths of earlier Imams, thereby refuting the 'Ghulat' (extremists) who claimed he was the Mahdi and would return. The passage emphasizes that such a prominent, documented event leaves no room for doubt, aligning with the Shia principle of clear historical evidence over speculative occultation.
